criteria.reasoning: The memo states "Director Thomas Aldana's spouse, Celeste M. Aldana, is the sole member (100% owner) of Saffron & Sage Events LLC". It concludes "Director Aldana had a clear Financial Interest in the catering contract."
The memo names both failures: "He answered 'No' to Question 2 on his annual statement", and he "made no disclosure when the Board Chair specifically asked for them at the February 12 meeting."

The memo says that "Instead of recusing himself as required by Article III, Section 3, Director Aldana actively advocated for Saffron & Sage". It adds that he "made the motion to award them the $68,400 contract, which passed 6–5 with his vote."

The memo says only that the motion "passed 6–5 with his vote." It never says that without his vote the result would have been a 5–5 tie that fails, so it does not address whether his vote decided the outcome.

The memo gives the "$68,400 contract" and notes "Saffron & Sage's base bid was $15,500 higher than the lowest bid". That correctly compares the price with the lowest bid. It does not name Harborview, but neither the bids nor the difference are misstated.

The memo finds "She fully complied". She disclosed on her annual statement, emailed the chair on February 2 and disclosed orally at the meeting, then "left the room, took no part in the vote", and the disinterested directors voted "10–0". The next steps address only Aldana, with no action recommended concerning her.

The memo states Saffron & Sage "meets the definition of an 'interested person' because it is more than 35% owned by a director's spouse" and that the transaction "must be reported on Schedule L". It notes the "$71,860" exceeds the $39,400 threshold.
The memo states the threshold is "the greater of $10,000 or 1% of the organization's total revenue". With revenue of "$3,940,000", that makes "the 1% threshold $39,400."

The memo treats BrightStage as an interested person (more than 35% owned by a director's brother). It concludes BrightStage need not be reported because "The Theatre paid BrightStage a total of $18,250 ... falling well below the $39,400 threshold."

Step 1 says "The Governance Committee must inform Director Aldana in writing of its reasonable cause to believe he failed to disclose the conflict" and give him "an opportunity to explain". This comes before board findings and possible discipline. The memo does not state that he deliberately concealed the interest.

Step 4 says "the disinterested directors must re-review the contract under Article III, Sections 3(c) and 3(d)". It adds that if the Theatre "paid more than fair market value", the Board "must consult legal counsel regarding whether the payment constitutes an excess benefit transaction under IRS Code Section 4958 and regarding the recovery of the excess funds."

The memo notes "Director Aldana currently serves on the Governance Committee". It says that under Article IV, Section 4 "he must take no part in the Committee's or the Board's deliberations or votes concerning his conduct."

The memo states the committee "must report its findings to the Board" and that "If a majority of disinterested directors determine he failed to disclose the conflict, they must take disciplinary or corrective action". It adds that he "must file a corrected annual conflict-of-interest statement within 30 days of the Board's determination."
